newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-LIPPI SET TO FIELD UNCHANGED TEAM AGAINST RIVER PLATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIPPI SET TO FIELD UNCHANGED TEAM AGAINST RIVER PLATE.

text.p: Juventus coach Marcello Lippi will almost certainly field the team that won a classic Champions' League match against Manchester United last Wednesday in Tuesday's World Club Cup final against River Plate of Argentina.

The ANSA news agency, reporting from Tokyo, said that Lippi was unlikely to change the side that beat United 1-0 at Old Trafford which secured their place in the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

Lippi rested Croat Alen Boksic from training ecause he has muscle fatigue but Boksic, who had a superb match against the English champions, should play. Zinedine Zidane, the first-half architect of Juventus' win in Manchester, also trained less than his team mates but again looks set to play.

"I'm satisfied," Lippi said. "The boys are in good form and have got over the jet lag. I think that against River Plate on Tuesday we are going to see a team that is determined, convinced of the great importance of this encounter."

River Plate trainer Ramon Diaz, who played for four Italian clubs in the 1980s -- Avellino, Napoli, Fiorentina, Inter -- said: "I think we can win, even if we aren't as famous as Juve my team is very highly motivated. We'll be out to show that South American soccer has no reason to feel envious of European soccer."

"I agree with Lippi when he says our teams are alike. I have some very technical players and it's not going to be us who turn the match into a scrap. We think we can win, even though we know it would certainly not be a dishonour to be beaten by Juventus."
Veteran Uruguayan international Enzo Francescoli will play from the start but Diaz still has to decide between Salas and Cruz up front.

South Amrerican teams have won three of the last four finals between the champions of Europe and South America and since the series started in 1960, they have won this fixture 20 times against Europe's 13.
Juventus: Angelo Peruzzi; Sergio Porrini, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Moreno Torricelli, Zinedine Zidane, Angelo di Livio, Didier Deschamps, Alen Boksic, Vladimir Jugovic, Alessandro del Piero
River Plate: Roberto Bonano, Hernan Diaz, Celso Ayala, Eduardo Berizzo, Juan Sorin, Roberto Montserrat, Leonardo Astrada, Sergio Berti, Ernzo Francescoli, Ariel Ortega, Julio Cruz.
